newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 4.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Friday and main factors likely to affect trading.

* Shares seen to continue their downward bias but a slight uptick later in the session would not come as a surprise as steep declines this week could result in a technical rebound, says Abacus Securities Corp manager Erwin Tan.

* Sun Hung Kai Securities Corp says in its daily market outlook that follow-through selling may continue as the 3,150 support has been broken, although accumulation might be seen as most issues have reached oversold levels.

* Abacus' Tan said release of March inflation figures may not affect the market because of expectations the report will be little changed compared to February's 4.4 percent level. The National Statistics Office is expected to release the figures at 9:00 a.m. (0100 GMT)

* The Philippine composite index closed sharply lower on Thursday by 57.44 points at 3,104.77. * Equitable Banking Corp which made its debut on Thursday is expected to continue being the focus of investors' attention.
* On Thursday, the Dow Jones shed 39.66 points to 6,477.35. PLDT's also closed lower by $0-1/4 to $59-3/8.
* San Miguel Corp announces its merger with Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd, creating the biggest Coca-Cola bottling group outside the United States.

* Megaworld Properties and Holdings Inc says it expects to post a 36 percent rise in first quarter 1997 net income at 500 million. Megaworld and its housing developer subsidiary Empire East Land Holdings Inc denied rumours that they are suffering from financial difficulties.
* RFM Corp says it sees first quarter 1997 net income at 220 million pesos from 97.1 million the same period last year.

* Most newspapers say the Department of Energy expects premium and regular gasoline prices to rise by 39 centavos per liter next week as a result of the rise in the regional trading prices of these products last month.
* Newspaper BusinessWorld said Equitable Bank will consolidate its non-allied investments under a one billion peso holding firm to be set up this year.
* The Philippine composite index closed sharply lower on Thursday by 57.44 points at 3,104.77.
* The peso closed steady at 26.370 to the dollar
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 9.9375 percent.
